newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher, boosted by aluminum.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher, boosted by aluminum.

text.p: COMEX copper ended higher on Wednesday, but dealings were rangebound and dull with gains gleaned for most part from a surge in aluminum futures to six-week highs on LME, traders said.
"Aluminum helped to drag copper up despite the spreads softening. Copper did not do anything independently," Bill O'Neill of Merrill Lynch said.
July COMEX copper settled 1.40 cents firmer at 110.45 cents per pound, traded 110.60 to 109.05 cents. Spot May went out 1.35 cents firmer at 111.10 cents. Volume was estimated at 6,500 lots.
The LME cash to three months premium or backwardation was largely steady at $62/$65.
The union representing striking workers at Chile's Quebrada Blanca copper mine said they doubted the company's assertion that the facility was still able to produce at half of its slated capacity.
Negotiations at the 75,000-tonne per year mine were still at a halt. Traders have said Quebrada's woes have already been largely priced into the market.

Meanwhile Phelps Dodge Corp said it planned to restart production at its historic Ajo copper mine in southern Arizona by spending $238 million on modernization with commercial output of 135 million pounds (61,235 tonnes) a year from late 1999 pending completion of environmental permits.
